title: Hazard Tree Removal & Flagstone Patio Rebuild
summary: A declining mesquite in a tiled courtyard was cracking the flagstone patio around it. Rather than patch around the problem, we took the tree down in sections, pulled the stump, tore out the entire damaged patio, and relaid it from scratch.

steps.caption: Rigging the mesquite with tag lines before cutting, to control where each section drops in a tight courtyard.
steps.alt: Crew member rigging a mesquite tree with tag lines before a hazard tree removal in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Working from the canopy down, cutting large limbs section by section away from the windows and stucco.
steps.alt: Crew member cutting large tree limbs from the canopy during a hazard tree removal in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Reduced to bare branches before the final cuts.
steps.alt: Mesquite tree reduced to bare branches during hazard tree removal in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Down to the stump, cut flush with the ground.
steps.alt: Tree stump cut flush to the ground after hazard tree removal on a Las Cruces courtyard patio

steps.caption: With the tree gone, the entire old flagstone patio came out too — broken up and hauled off.
steps.alt: Old flagstone patio demolished into rubble around a fresh-cut tree stump in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: The root system running under the patio, right at the door — the real reason it needed to come out.
steps.alt: Exposed tree root system running under a demolished flagstone patio near a doorway in Las Cruces

steps.caption: Laser level and string lines mark the new patio before the first stone goes down.
steps.alt: Laser level and string lines laying out a new flagstone patio base in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Fresh flagstone delivered by the pallet for the new patio.
steps.alt: Pallet of new flagstone delivered by flatbed truck for a Las Cruces patio rebuild

steps.alt: New flagstone being set in mortar near French doors during a Las Cruces patio rebuild

steps.caption: A quick look at the flagstone going down.
steps.alt: Video of crew setting new flagstone during a Las Cruces patio rebuild

steps.caption: The finished courtyard — new flagstone throughout, grouted and clean.
steps.alt: Finished flagstone courtyard patio with vine-covered archway at a Las Cruces home

steps.caption: And the kiva fireplace corner, with the tree that used to crack it gone for good.
steps.alt: Finished flagstone patio with kiva fireplace at a Las Cruces home

title: Erosion-Control Drainage Channel
summary: Monsoon runoff was cutting a rough wash across a large desert lot toward the house. We marked a proper channel, graded it, and lined the whole run with river rock over fabric so heavy rain has somewhere controlled to go.

steps.caption: The lot before work started — established desert plantings with an unmanaged wash running through it.
steps.alt: Desert lot with established native plantings before a drainage channel installation in Las Cruces

steps.caption: Marking the new channel path with paint before any digging starts.
steps.alt: Spray-painted layout line marking a new drainage channel path through desert landscaping

steps.caption: Grading the channel bed so water has a clear, controlled path to follow.
steps.alt: Freshly graded sandy channel bed during excavation for a drainage project in Las Cruces

steps.caption: Fabric down first to keep the base stable, then river rock loaded in section by section.
steps.alt: Landscape fabric and river rock being placed at the start of a drainage channel installation

steps.caption: Rock placement continuing along the run, past the utility box toward the house.
steps.alt: River rock drainage channel under construction running past a utility box in a desert yard

steps.caption: The channel taking shape — a clean, continuous rock-lined path through the property.
steps.alt: Nearly finished river rock drainage channel winding through desert landscaping in Las Cruces

steps.caption: The finished channel, ready for the next monsoon — water now has somewhere to go instead of cutting new washes.
steps.alt: Finished river rock drainage channel through a desert landscape with mountain views in Las Cruces

title: Mature Backyard Xeriscape
summary: A fully established xeriscape backyard — dry creek bed, boulder accents, tan gravel, and ornamental grasses — built for zero-lawn water savings without giving up a lived-in backyard feel.

steps.caption: The dry creek bed and stone perimeter wall, the anchor feature of the yard.
steps.alt: Dry creek bed with river rock and boulders along a natural stone perimeter wall in a Las Cruces backyard xeriscape

steps.caption: The full yard from the covered patio — tan gravel, ornamental grasses, and accent boulders, no turf to water.
steps.alt: Covered patio overlooking a tan gravel xeriscape yard with ornamental grasses and accent boulders
